advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Move the mcp memory pre-check before the build+tag so a memory-bound box aborts without rebuilding the image on every retry.
evidence: infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh:632: `if ! ( cd "$COMPOSE_DIR" && docker compose build mcp ); then`
infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh:641: `mcp_mem="$(mcp_mem_available_mb)"`
Comment at :639 claims 'memory pre-check BEFORE the 2x overlap' — true w.r.t. the second container, but the build/tag/rsync have already consumed CPU, disk and cache before the gate.
advisory.finding: The memory pre-check (step 2) runs AFTER the immutable image build+tag (step 1), so on a persistently memory-bound box every backoff retry re-runs `docker compose build mcp` (and the rsync) only to abort at the memory gate — the exact expensive work the abort is meant to avoid on an 8GiB box, repeated on each capped-backoff tick.
advisory.suggested_fix: Perform the mcp_mem_available_mb check immediately after `changed "$MCP_PATHS"` (before checkout/rsync/build), emitting AUTODEPLOY_MCP_MEM_ABORT and backing off prior to any build work.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Capture stderr of the failed `docker run` (bounded/redacted) into the deploy journal on mcp-run-failed, mirroring capture_bot_logs.
evidence: infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh:367: `"$MCP_IMAGE:$TARGET" >/dev/null 2>&1`
infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh:658-659: on failure only `err mcp-run-failed "docker run $mcp_newname on 127.0.0.1:${mcp_newport} failed"` is emitted
Contrast infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh:237-245 capture_bot_logs, which captures the container's own output before rollback so 'broken image' vs 'slow start' can be distinguished.
advisory.finding: mcp_run_new redirects all `docker run` output to /dev/null, so when the NEW container fails to start the deploy emits only a generic `mcp-run-failed` marker with no captured docker error — a diagnostic blind spot the review-bot path deliberately avoids with capture_bot_logs.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Decide whether an mcp blast-radius violation should be fatal (record_backoff_failure + exit) rather than advisory, consistent with the fail-closed-gate stability intent.
evidence: infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh:692-694: `if [ -n "$gerrit_before_mcp" ] && [ "$gerrit_before_mcp" != "$gerrit_after_mcp" ]; then err blast-radius ... fi`
No `record_backoff_failure`/`exit 1` in that branch; control falls through to :695 prune + :696 success log.
Same pattern exists in the reviewbot block (:604-608), so this is a pre-existing convention rather than new — noting for consistency.
advisory.finding: The blast-radius assertion for the mcp deploy emits `err blast-radius` (an AUTODEPLOY_ERROR marker) if the gerrit container id changed, but does NOT record_backoff_failure or exit non-zero, so the deploy still falls through to success, advances deployed-sha, and logs 'mcp redeployed + healthy' — the same non-fatal treatment as the bot path, but here it follows a completed cutover that could have collaterally disrupted gerrit.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Treat an unreadable port for a running managed container as 'assume-bound' (or emit a distinct marker) rather than silently excluding it from the bound set in mcp_free_port.
evidence: infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh:332: `p="$(mcp_port_of "$n")"; [ -n "$p" ] && bound="$bound $p"` — a container whose port cannot be read is silently excluded from `bound`.
infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh:308: `mcp_port_of` echoes nothing on any docker error (2>/dev/null).
advisory.finding: mcp_free_port returns empty both when both ports are legitimately occupied AND if `mcp_port_of` fails to read a running container's port (e.g. `docker port` transiently errors), because an unreadable port simply omits it from `bound`, potentially causing a free-port pick that collides — conversely a container that IS bound but whose port is unreadable is treated as NOT bound, so the deploy could `docker run -p` onto a port already in use and fail at the docker layer.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the `--restart always` blue/green containers with reboot behavior so a host/daemon restart cannot re-bind stale mcp ports or leave the /mcp upstream pointing at a wrong-SHA backend.
evidence: infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh:348 `    --restart always \`

mcp_retire_graceful issues `docker stop --time` but never `docker rm` (autodeploy.sh:~mcp_retire_graceful); reaping only happens for exited containers in mcp_retire_sweep: `docker rm "$n" ... && log "mcp retire: reaped exited $n"`

Docker restarts containers with restart policy `always` on daemon start even if they were manually stopped (only `unless-stopped` honors a manual stop), so a retired-but-unreaped blue/green container re-binds its host port after reboot
autodeploy.sh:340-345 comment: "`docker compose up mcp` pins host 8091 and would collide ... so every env value is spelled out here"
mcp_run_new uses raw `docker run -d --name "$1"` (autodeploy.sh:347), not `docker compose`, so the container carries no compose project/service labels
compose-up.sh has no matches for `restart` and does not know about the autodeploy-managed rebar-mcp-* containers
docker-compose.yml:382-383 `    logging:` / `      driver: journald`
mcp_run_new (autodeploy.sh:347-372) sets `--restart always`, `--stop-timeout`, `--env-file`, `-e`, `-p`, `-v` but no `--log-driver journald`
test_docker_run_matches_compose_mcp_service (tests/scripts/test_autodeploy_mcp_bluegreen.py:724-765) asserts env, volumes, --env-file, --restart always, --stop-timeout 1260 but not the log driver
advisory.finding: Blue/green mcp containers are started with `--restart always` but retired OLD containers are only `docker rm`'d once exited, so on a host/daemon reboot Docker re-launches every `--restart always` mcp container (including manually-stopped `always` ones and both blue/green ports), re-binding host ports 8092/8093 while the compose-managed `compose-mcp-1` also comes up on 8091 — leaving the post-reboot live mcp version undefined and the nginx upstream possibly pointing at a container whose image no longer reflects the flipped SHA.
merged_from: The blue/green mcp containers are created via `docker run` outside compose (project 'compose'), so they are not part of `docker compose` state — an operator `docker compose down`/`up` or the boot compose-up.sh neither manages nor reaps them, and they can leak alongside the compose-managed `compose-mcp-1`.

mcp_run_new does not reproduce the compose service's `logging: driver: journald`, so the blue/green container defaults to json-file logging — diverging from the compose mcp service and the journald-centric observability posture; the compose-parity test asserts env/mounts/restart/stop-timeout but not the logging driver, so this drift is uncaught.
scenarios: Host/EC2 reboot or dockerd restart after one or more blue/green cutovers with un-reaped old containers
compose-up.sh brings up compose-mcp-1 on 8091 while a restarted blue/green container holds 8092/8093 and nginx points at a stale port
advisory.suggested_fix: Use `--restart unless-stopped` (so a graceful `docker stop` survives a daemon restart), and/or `docker rm` the old container after its graceful stop completes, and have compose-up.sh reconcile the /mcp upstream to the compose-managed backend on boot.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Prune retired `compose-mcp:<sha>` image tags (beyond MCP_RELEASES_KEEP) so old immutable mcp releases do not accumulate on the root disk.
evidence: autodeploy.sh:625-627 `docker tag "$MCP_IMAGE" "$MCP_IMAGE:$TARGET"` on every deploy
MCP_RELEASES_KEEP/CAP govern container count, not images; no `docker image rm`/`docker image prune` of old `compose-mcp:<sha>` tags appears in the diff
monitoring_autodeploy.tf:190-215 documents root-disk exhaustion (incident 2731) fail-closing every review — the disk this accumulates on
advisory.finding: Each mcp deploy tags a new immutable image `compose-mcp:<sha>` but nothing ever removes prior SHA-tagged images; because they are tagged (not dangling), prune_docker_caches / `docker builder prune` will not reclaim them, so mcp images accumulate on the 30G root disk over successive deploys.
scenarios: Many mcp deploys over weeks, each leaving a retained compose-mcp:<sha> image
Root disk pressure alarm (root_disk_used_percent) trips from tagged-image accumulation
advisory.suggested_fix: After a successful cutover, `docker image rm` (or an explicit tag-retention sweep) old `compose-mcp:<sha>` tags not backing a live/kept container.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test where `docker run` (mcp_run_new) exits nonzero and assert the new container is `docker rm -f`ed, AUTODEPLOY_ERROR/mcp-run-failed is emitted, rc!=0, and deployed-sha is unchanged.
evidence: autodeploy.sh:658-661: `if ! mcp_run_new "$mcp_newname" "$mcp_newport"; then err mcp-run-failed ...; docker rm -f "$mcp_newname" ...; record_backoff_failure; exit 1`

Named violating input: docker run exits nonzero (e.g. `$MCP_IMAGE:$TARGET` tag absent). The docker stub always `exit 0`s on `run` (`_DOCKER_STUB`: `run) ... exit 0 ;;`), so this branch is never entered by any test.
The suite tests health-failure rollback (test_unhealthy_new_container...) and flip-failure rollback (test_nginx_reload_failure...) but has no run-failure case.
autodeploy.sh:382: `if ! nginx -t >/dev/null 2>&1 || ! nginx -s reload >/dev/null 2>&1; then` — a validate failure and a reload failure are distinct triggers of the same rollback.
test_nginx_reload_failure_restores_the_previous_upstream builds the box with `nginx_reload_rc=1`; no test passes `nginx_t_rc=1`.
The stub parameter exists (`_write_common_stubs(... nginx_t_rc: int = 0 ...)`) but is unused with a non-zero value anywhere.
advisory.finding: The step-4 `mcp-run-failed` rollback contract is untested: when `mcp_run_new` returns nonzero the code removes the just-started container with `docker rm -f` and backs off (autodeploy.sh:658-661), but no test drives docker run to a nonzero exit, so the cleanup+backoff+non-advance-of-deployed-sha behavior is unverified.
merged_from: The `nginx -t` (config validate) failure branch of `mcp_flip_upstream` is not independently exercised: `_write_common_stubs` accepts `nginx_t_rc` but no test sets it non-zero — only the reload-failure path (nginx_reload_rc=1) is tested.
scenarios: A blue-green deploy where the newly-tagged mcp image fails to start; the deploy must remove the orphaned container, back off, and not advance deployed-sha.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a docker-stub variant whose `run` case exits nonzero (or an env-gated failure) and assert the rm-f + backoff + unchanged deployed-sha contract, mirroring test_unhealthy_new_container_leaves_old_upstream_current.
